title: Maintain a project's semantic repository service
summary: Install, maintain, recover, or uninstall Semantics and its serial Clockwork worker. Register, seed, pause, resume, or route projects, and manage deployment holds.
use_when: Semantics should be installed, updated, diagnosed, or uninstalled for this macOS user.
A folder should join, move within, pause, resume, or retire from the project registry.
Existing vocabulary should be seeded, intake should be inspected or manually routed, or a failed reconciliation should be recovered.
do_not_use_when: Only repository terminology should be read; use semantics.repository.explore.
Registration or a move targets a folder without an exact root AGENTS.md participation marker.
Retained state should be deleted; uninstall intentionally retains it.
outcome: A managed installation and explicit project registry whose repositories are maintained by agents interpreting post-activation documents from one Annals decisions library.
effects: Authorized procedures can change project/intake state, prepare a restricted reconciliation job, or install/migrate/publish the matching product release. Required features own the detailed effect and consistency guarantees.
Install/recovery preserves proved state and captured admission; uninstall removes owned installation surfaces while retaining state.
authority: Semantics owns project identity, routing, cursor persistence, intake transitions, stable concept IDs, typed-effect validation, and the SQLite commit.

Annals owns accepted document bytes, library identity, acceptance order and cursors. Nucleus owns execution and mailbox transport. Clockwork owns activation. Semantics owns project intake and the semantic commit; the agent interprets relevance under its instructions.
A participating project's source and tests remain runtime authority; its root AGENTS.md owns participation instructions.
success: Verify the selected project or intake result in Semantics records; require green doctor and exact owned command/provider/binding selection for installation.
Preserve captured schedule intent and all unrelated pauses, incident halts, and holds.
failure_and_recovery: Stop on failing prerequisites, active or unproved prior jobs, foreign artifacts, changed ownership evidence, or unproved recovery.
Use the exact retained transaction and the semantics.service recovery rules. Keep maintenance on uncertainty; never manufacture cursors, clear correlations, or discard a committed result.
Resolve product work separately from explicit approval to resume a Clockwork incident.
privacy: Treat selected source/repository/job evidence, paths, state, and backups as private. Required features define each exposure and retention boundary.
Inspect body-free logs and bounded runtime metadata; keep source bodies and raw dependency diagnostics out of service logs.
steps: Read the required Semantics feature contracts and shared Nucleus operator manual. Inspect the exact Annals decisions library, Nucleus, Clockwork, retained state, prompt selection, and owned publication. Inspect Conversations only for retained historical jobs that require it.
For deployment, build a green candidate and run the content-addressed deployer; verify doctor and all owned selectors before registering projects.

Add the exact Semantics-Project marker to the project's root AGENTS.md, register the canonical folder at the current watermark, and seed only existing authoritative vocabulary when needed; after verifying HEAD, the source file may be separately removed under normal project authority.
Inspect repository HEAD, intake state, the one-shot worker report, Clockwork binding and activation history, and body-free product logs before relying on periodic maintenance.
Pause before maintenance; resume only after markers and dependencies are healthy. Uninstall only with the retained-state boundary understood.
checkpoints: Registration and moves require an exact line in a regular root AGENTS.md; nested or approximate markers do not participate.

Registration captures the current Annals watermark; moves preserve cursor histories. Each new document becomes separate intake for each participating project after its own activation point, with relevance decided by its agent.

Before candidate access, verify owned release/selector/marker/log evidence, suspend public work and scheduling, hold the worker flock, prove SQLite closed, and privately back up database plus sidecars. Retain authenticated holds and recovery evidence under the semantics.service rules.
Nucleus receives the handed document and repository with workspace none, no shell, and no web. No additional source lookup or metadata is required. Semantics owns the commit transaction.

Retirement requires a paused project. Pending or paused intake with zero attempts and no retained Nucleus request becomes ignored with reason project_retired in the same transaction. Other unresolved intake blocks retirement without changing state. Source bytes, repository history, and cursors remain retained; the old folder may be absent.
adaptation: Manual assignment remains for historical unassigned intake. New documents are offered to project agents, which can return no change.

Seed one project-local definition-list document only at revision 0; after verifying HEAD, the source may be removed because replay uses committed effects while retaining its relative label and SHA-256 digest.
For an alternate test home, pass explicit --home and --launchctl only within an isolated synthetic boundary.
stop_when: Annals exchange 2 or Nucleus execution 3 is unavailable, or required doctor checks fail. Conversation metadata is not a new-document prerequisite.
A selector, release, plist, database, sidecar, marker, or registered root is foreign, symbolic where a regular path is required, ambiguous, or cannot be safely rolled back.
The requested action would delete retained state, manufacture a cursor, expose repository bodies in logs, or let Nucleus bypass Semantics validation.
does_not_authorize: Deleting retained database, releases, logs, or project files.
Reading upstream or Semantics SQLite directly, parsing cursors, or mutating Annals, Conversations, Nucleus, Codex, or project runtime state.
Treating model output or Nucleus completion as a semantic commit.

consumers.statement: An authorized local operator may install, maintain, recover, or uninstall Semantics and maintain selected participating projects through the documented procedures.

preconditions.statement: Read required feature contracts and shared coordination guidance. Select exact state, project, dependency configuration and job/transaction identities; prove ownership, readiness and quiescence before consequential effects.

inputs.statement: Inputs are the intended authorized action, exact selected project/intake/installation, matching validated candidate artifacts, captured admission intent, run ID, or retained recovery transaction. Explicit legacy cutover additionally requires its captured final watermark and external gates.

outputs.statement: Output is the selected operation receipt, project/intake/repository result, readiness report, or exact installation/recovery evidence interpreted under the required feature contracts.

data_semantics.statement: Semantics domain results, Nucleus runtime state, Clockwork activation/incident state and captured admission intent remain separate. Verify the authority that owns the requested result.

identity_and_units.statement: Select exact project, upstream source, requester/job, release, definition, run owner or transaction identities before action. The required features own their formats and meanings.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Verification covers the selected operation and its consequential effects, retained state, required prerequisites, and captured admission intent.
No wall-clock bound from an upstream decision to a semantic revision is promised.

access.statement: Procedures use local-user supported commands, exact owned files, and the selected private state. Required features define dependency access and model isolation.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Follow required feature invariants and product-owned commit/recovery boundaries. Pause before semantic maintenance, settle admitted work, preserve foreign holds and incident halts, and release only this operation ownership.

operational_limits.statement: Use bootstrap seed only at revision 0, explicit retry only after positive prior-job terminal evidence, and legacy activation only through the documented gated one-time installer procedure.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Operation contract 9 and existing operating routes are unchanged. Required features consolidate the previously distributed explanation; provider release, persistent schema, immutable requests, and entry contracts retain separate versions.

reliances.statement: This operation relies on Semantics feature contracts for exact project, replay, reconciliation and installation guarantees.
Selected procedures consume complete documents and opaque cursors from the exact configured Annals library.
Selected reconciliation and diagnostic procedures use Nucleus while Semantics retains domain authority.
Selected installation and incident procedures use Clockwork-owned schedule and halt controls.
Semantics promises no launchd availability or worker wake-up latency beyond Clockwork observations.
Prompt update and preparation use pinned Bazaar strings while Semantics retains selection and execution authority.
